body.en: The imaginary unit \( i \) extends the reals; complex numbers add, multiply, and have a modulus and conjugate.
\( i^{2}=-1 \); \( z=a+bi \) has modulus \( |z|=\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}} \) and conjugate \( \bar{z}=a-bi \), with \( z\bar{z}=|z|^{2} \).

Algebraic & Geometric Duality of \(\mathbb{C}\): Every complex number \(z = x + iy\) corresponds bijectively to a point \((x, y)\) in the Argand plane with modulus \(r = |z| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\) and principal argument \(\theta = \arg(z) \in (-\pi, \pi]\). In exponential Euler form, \(z = re^{i\theta} = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\), multiplication scales moduli and adds arguments: \(z_1 z_2 = r_1 r_2 e^{i(\theta_1 + \theta_2)}\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Complex Numbers)

body.en:
Why De Moivre's Theorem & Conjugate Root Pairing Hold: By Euler's identity \(e^{i\theta} = \cos\theta + i\sin\theta\), raising \(z = re^{i\theta}\) to the \(n\)-th power gives:

\[ z^n = \left(re^{i\theta}\right)^n = r^n e^{in\theta} = r^n(\cos(n\theta) + i\sin(n\theta)) \]

Furthermore, if \(P(z) = \sum_{k=0}^n a_k z^k\) has real coefficients (\(a_k \in \mathbb{R}\)), taking complex conjugates across \(P(z_0) = 0\) uses \(\overline{z_1 + z_2} = \bar{z}_1 + \bar{z}_2\) and \(\bar{a}_k = a_k\) to prove \(P(\bar{z}_0) = \overline{P(z_0)} = 0\). Thus non-real roots of real polynomials always occur in conjugate pairs \(\alpha \pm i\beta\).

Write \(z=-1+\sqrt{3}\,i\) in modulus-argument form and find \(z^4\) using De Moivre's theorem.

\(|z|=\sqrt{1+3}=2\). \(\arg z=\pi-\arctan\sqrt{3}=\pi-\tfrac{\pi}{3}=\tfrac{2\pi}{3}\).

\(z=2\bigl(\cos\tfrac{2\pi}{3}+i\sin\tfrac{2\pi}{3}\bigr)\). By De Moivre: \(z^4=2^4\bigl(\cos\tfrac{8\pi}{3}+i\sin\tfrac{8\pi}{3}\bigr)=16\bigl(\cos\tfrac{2\pi}{3}+i\sin\tfrac{2\pi}{3}\bigr)=16(-\tfrac{1}{2}+\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}i)=-8+8\sqrt3\,i\).

Problem (Medium): Given \( \log_b 3=A \) and \( \log_b 2=B \), express \( \log_b 216 \) in terms of A and B.

Step-by-Step Solution: \( 216=3^{3}\cdot 2^{3} \Rightarrow \log_b 216=3A+3B \).

Problem (Hard): Given \( f(x)=x-6 \), evaluate \( |f(1)| \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Applying Functions: Modulus & Inverse principles, \( f(1)=-5 \), so \( |f(1)|=5 \). Therefore, the verified correct option is 5.

body.en: Exam Verification Tip (Cambridge International A Level (9709 Paper 3 / Paper 6)): Always check complex division \(\dfrac{z_1}{z_2}\) by verifying that \(|z_1 / z_2| = |z_1| / |z_2|\). If the moduli ratio does not match, you multiplied the denominator by \(a + bi\) instead of the conjugate \(a - bi\).

label.en: ⚠️ Cambridge 9709 Traps — Principal Argument Interval & Geometric Loci

body.en:
Principal Argument Range: Cambridge 9709 requires the principal argument to satisfy \(-\pi < \arg(z) \le \pi\). When \(z\) lies in Quadrant 2 (\(x < 0, y > 0\)), \(\arg(z) = \pi - \arctan(|y/x|)\). In Quadrant 3 (\(x < 0, y < 0\)), \(\arg(z) = -(\pi - \arctan(|y/x|))\). Blindly using \(\arctan(y/x)\) on a calculator yields the wrong quadrant.

Standard Geometric Loci:

  • \(|z - z_1| = r\): Circle of radius \(r\) centred at \(z_1\).
  • \(|z - z_1| = |z - z_2|\): Perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining \(z_1\) and \(z_2\).
  • \(\arg(z - z_1) = \alpha\): Half-line starting from (but not including) \(z_1\) at angle \(\alpha\) to the positive real direction.

question.en: On an Argand diagram, the point \(P\) represents the complex number \(z\) such that \(|z - (2 + 3i)| \le 2\). Find the greatest possible value of \(|z|\) for points in this region.

solution.en:
The locus \(|z - (2 + 3i)| \le 2\) represents a circular disc of radius \(R = 2\) with center at \(C(2, 3)\).

The distance from the origin \(O(0, 0)\) to the center \(C\) is:

\[|C| = \sqrt{2^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{4 + 9} = \sqrt{13} \approx 3.6055\]

The point on the disc farthest from the origin lies on the line passing through \(O\) and \(C\), on the far boundary of the circle:

\[|z|_{\max} = |C| + R = \sqrt{13} + 2 \approx 3.606 + 2 = 5.61\text{ (3 s.f.)}\]

hints.en: The locus \(|z - (2 + 3i)| \le 2\) represents a circular disc of radius \(R = 2\) with center at \(C(2, 3)\).
The distance from the origin \(O(0, 0)\) to the center \(C\) is: \(|C| = \sqrt{2^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{4 + 9} = \sqrt{13}\).
The point on the disc farthest from the origin lies on the line passing through \(O\) and \(C\), on the far boundary of the circle: \(|z|_{\max} = |C| + R = \sqrt{13} + 2 = 3.606 + 2\).

question.en: [Practice 3 · Easy] The complex number \( z \) is given by \[ z = \frac{4 + 3\mathrm{i}}{2 - \mathrm{i}}. \] Express \( z \) in the Cartesian form \( x + \mathrm{i}y \), where \( x \) and \( y \) are real numbers.

hints.en: To express \( z \) in the form \( x + \mathrm{i}y \), multiply the numerator and the denominator by the complex conjugate of the denominator.
The denominator is \( 2 - \mathrm{i} \), so its complex conjugate is \( 2 + \mathrm{i} \).
Divide the numerator by the denominator: \(z = \frac{5 + 10\mathrm{i}}{5}\).

solution.en:
To express \( z \) in the form \( x + \mathrm{i}y \), multiply the numerator and the denominator by the complex conjugate of the denominator.

The denominator is \( 2 - \mathrm{i} \), so its complex conjugate is \( 2 + \mathrm{i} \).

Multiply numerator and denominator:
\[ z = \frac{(4 + 3\mathrm{i})(2 + \mathrm{i})}{(2 - \mathrm{i})(2 + \mathrm{i})} \]

Expand the numerator:
\[ (4 + 3\mathrm{i})(2 + \mathrm{i}) = 8 + 4\mathrm{i} + 6\mathrm{i} + 3\mathrm{i}^2 = 8 + 10\mathrm{i} - 3 = 5 + 10\mathrm{i} \]

Expand the denominator:
\[ (2 - \mathrm{i})(2 + \mathrm{i}) = 2^2 - \mathrm{i}^2 = 4 - (-1) = 5 \]

Divide the numerator by the denominator:
\[ z = \frac{5 + 10\mathrm{i}}{5} = 1 + 2\mathrm{i} \]

Common errors:
- \( 1 - 2\mathrm{i} \) results from an inadvertent sign flip in the imaginary term (taking the conjugate of the answer).
- \( \frac{11}{5} + \frac{2}{5}\mathrm{i} \) results from mistakenly multiplying the numerator by \( 2 - \mathrm{i} \) instead of the conjugate \( 2 + \mathrm{i} \).
- \( 5 + 10\mathrm{i} \) results from expanding the numerator correctly but omitting the division by the real denominator \( 5 \).

question.en: [Practice 4 · Medium] Solve \( e^{2x}-27e^x+140=0 \) for \( x \). Give the larger solution in exact form.

solution.en: \( (e^x-7)(e^x-20)=0 \Rightarrow e^x=7 \) or \( e^x=20 \Rightarrow x=\ln 7 \) or \( x=\ln 20 \). Larger: \( x=\ln 20 \).
